title: Unique one-sided K-flat tensor comparison normalized by two-sided descent
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention] and $B$ a sheaf of commutative rings, with module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $K(B)$ be their homotopy category and $Q:K(B)\to D(B)$ localization at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\mathcal P_B$ be the full subcategory of K-flat complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex] with flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Use total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and fix the derived tensor and its specified two-sided comparison from [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], written
$$\delta_{T,V}:Q\operatorname{Tot}(T\otimes_B V)\xrightarrow{\sim}QT\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}QV\quad(T,V\in\mathcal P_B).$$
For every $T\in\mathcal P_B$, both total tensor functors with fixed factor $T$ preserve quasi-isomorphisms of arbitrary complexes. There is a unique family of isomorphisms
$$c_{T,M}:QT\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}QM\xrightarrow{\sim}Q\operatorname{Tot}(T\otimes_B M)\quad(T\in\mathcal P_B,\ M\in K(B))$$
which is natural in $M$ and satisfies $c_{T,V}=\delta_{T,V}^{-1}$ for every $V\in\mathcal P_B$. This family is also natural in every homotopy-category map $T\to T'$ between objects of $\mathcal P_B$. Explicitly, for every homotopy-category map $f:M\to M'$,
$$Q(1_T\otimes f)\,c_{T,M}=c_{T,M'}(1_{QT}\otimes^{\mathbf L}Qf),$$
and for every $g:T\to T'$,
$$Q(g\otimes1_M)\,c_{T,M}=c_{T',M}(Qg\otimes^{\mathbf L}1_{QM}).$$
Here composition is written right to left. In particular the first equation holds for every K-flat flat-term resolution $V\to M$ and determines the comparison from its specified two-sided normalization. The analogous assertion for $M\otimes_B T$ holds with normalization supplied by the same two-sided comparison in that order; the chain symmetry interchanging factors has component $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{ij}y\otimes x$ in bidegree $(i,j)$. The complex $M$ need not be K-flat, termwise flat, or bounded.

proof.text: For each homotopy object X apply lem-pc-kflat-resolution to X.as, and convert its termwise exact tensor-right functors to IsFlatOnSite using siteSheafTensorRightIso from lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits. This gives a quasi-isomorphism r:V→X with V in the supplied P. The predicate supplied by lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent equals P by their membership equivalences. Transport its localization equivalence to conclude that L=P.ι⋙Q is a localization at the restricted quasi-isomorphisms.

Take a chain representative of a homotopy quasi-isomorphism f. Apply the quasi-isomorphism-preservation clause of lem-weil-pbc-kflat-fixed-tensor-triangulated to the fixed complex T.as. The specified hB natural isomorphism identifies both resulting quotient tensor maps with the maps of the supplied B, by its naturality squares. Quasi-isomorphisms respect arrow isomorphisms, proving preservation for both orders.

For fixed T put F=D(QT,-) and H=B(T,-)⋙Q. Step 2 lets H descend along Q to H′, with φ:Q⋙H′≅H. The inverse of δ restricted to (T,V) is a natural isomorphism e:L⋙F≅P.ι⋙H. Compose e with the inverse of P.ι-whiskered φ. Fully faithful precomposition by L, from lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property, lifts this isomorphism to b:F≅H′. Define c=(Q-whiskered b) followed by φ. The preimage equation and cancellation of φ give c(V)=δ(T,V)⁻¹ exactly.

Two natural transformations Q⋙F→H equal on P agree everywhere: choose r:V→X from step 1; naturality and cancellation of the isomorphism F(Qr) force equality at X. Apply this first to the hom transformations of normalized comparison families, proving uniqueness. For g:T→T′ apply it to c(T) followed by Q(B(g,-)) and D(Qg,-) followed by c(T′). Their equality on P is exactly naturality of δ inverse at (g,idV). This proves naturality in every fixed-factor map without inverting g.

Apply the same one-order argument to the flipped bifunctors B.flip and D.flip with comparison δ(V,T). This proves all reversed-order clauses. The final signed summand formula is precisely the existing CochainComplex.Monoidal.ι_braiding_hom lemma for the tensor on module sheaves.

tool_uses.why: The fixed two-sided site tensor and resolving-subcategory localization are the datum to normalize; no geometric Kunneth node supplies this foundational universal property.
Extends functors and natural isomorphisms along the two localization functors; a generic categorical tool, not a replacement for the geometric unit route.
The cone criterion in the abelian module category lets the K-flat acyclicity definition prove quasi-isomorphism preservation.
Identifies the cone of the tensor map with tensor of the cone on an arbitrary ringed site.
Provides a flat-term K-flat resolution of every arbitrary unbounded complex, used in uniqueness and simultaneous naturality.
